image.subject: A freckled, sandy-haired 12-year-old boy in a faded blue cotton shirt with patched knee trousers and bare feet, a grin that is half mischief, a tin bucket in hand, standing on a dusty St. Petersburg street at sunset with a whitewashed picket fence behind him.

storyboard.claim: Tom's theatrical world, where he controls every variable, is about to hit reality.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Tom with his bucket on a dusty street at sunset, the confident grin still on his face.
storyboard.onScreenText: THE PLAY ENDS / STAGE MANAGE / ROBIN HOOD
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the spin-economy close of the last chunk; now the play is ending.
storyboard.addedInformation: Tom is still in full control of his own fantasy at this point.

image.subject: The timber steps of the county courthouse in St. Petersburg at dusk, a knot of grave townspeople in dark 1840s coats and bonnets standing in the fading light.

storyboard.claim: The play economy is about to shatter against the adult world.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The courthouse steps at dusk with serious townspeople gathered.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Tom's make-believe is contrasted with the sober adult town.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the adult institutions that will judge the boys' secret.

image.subject: Tom Sawyer and Huck Finn stand at the gate of a dark graveyard at midnight, a lantern-less road stretching back toward distant town lights, a dead cat tied in a rag hanging from Huck's hand.

storyboard.claim: The boys are a mile and a half from town at a graveyard at midnight.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two boys at a dark graveyard gate, a dead cat in a rag, distant town lights.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The Halloween play moves from the street to the graveyard.
storyboard.addedInformation: Distance from town signals isolation.

image.subject: A crazy board fence leaning inward at a graveyard edge, round-topped boards gnawed by weather, staggering over sunken grave mounds in pitch darkness lit only by a thin moon.

storyboard.claim: The graveyard is pitch black with a fence leaning inward over sunken graves.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A leaning board fence over sunken mounds under a thin moon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the approach to the graveyard.
storyboard.addedInformation: Decay and unease in the setting.

image.subject: Two boys crouched close together behind a leaning tombstone in a dark graveyard, a dead elm bending in the wind above them, the wind moaning through its branches.

storyboard.claim: Tom and Huck are huddled and terrified in the graveyard.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two crouched boys behind a tombstone under a bending dead elm.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The fear builds from the fence to the boys themselves.
storyboard.addedInformation: The wind and the dead elm supply the eerie mood.

image.subject: A dead grey tabby cat lying on a flat grave slab under moonlight in an old graveyard, a rag and a short cord beside it, the superstition of a midnight cure.

storyboard.claim: They have a dead cat and are trying to cure warts with a childhood superstition.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A dead cat on a grave slab in moonlight with a rag and cord beside it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The boys' midnight errand is explained.
storyboard.addedInformation: The superstition is shown as a literal prop.

image.subject: Three dim figures approaching along a graveyard path through the gloom, one of them swinging an old-fashioned tin lantern whose light trembles over leaning wooden grave markers, seen from behind a clump of brush.

storyboard.claim: Voices and vague figures approach, swinging a tin lantern.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Three dim figures on a graveyard path, one with a swinging tin lantern.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The boys' hiding turns into the moment of hearing voices.
storyboard.addedInformation: The lantern is the only light and the first clue of approaching men.

storyboard.claim: The boys think it is devils or the ghost of Hos Williams.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A question card asking whether they are devils or a ghost.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The lantern's light spreads on the ground, so the boys assume the supernatural.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the boys' superstition as a question.

image.subject: A pair of bare boy's feet in the dirt at the edge of a lantern's circle of light, poised to bolt into the dark brush, a tangle of weeds behind them.

storyboard.claim: Childhood fantasy meets harsh adult reality.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Bare feet at the lantern's edge, poised to run.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The voices turn fear into the moment of collision.
storyboard.addedInformation: Connects the boys' childhood to the adult danger.

left.label: THE PLAY
left.subject: A barefoot boy in a homemade paper hat waving a stick like a sword on a sunny dusty street, grinning at an audience of other boys.

right.label: THE TOWN
right.subject: Townspeople in black Sunday clothes gathered at a white church door in the summer sun, sombre and unconvinced.

storyboard.claim: Tom has conned his way out of chores and staged his own funeral; he is master of the play.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A boy playing a sword game against a sombre Sunday crowd.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The earlier fantasy is set against the adult town.
storyboard.addedInformation: Tom's spin is contrasted with the town's grave reality.

image.subject: A rusted clasp knife and a lead musket ball lying on a rough plank table in a dim room, a single tallow candle burning beside them.

storyboard.claim: You cannot negotiate with a bullet or a knife.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A knife and a musket ball on a table beside a candle.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The fantasy has no power against real weapons.
storyboard.addedInformation: Real danger replaces the play economy's negotiation.

image.subject: A thin, barefoot 13-year-old boy in ragged homespun clothes, a battered straw hat with a torn brim, dirt on his face and a sly, watchful expression, crouched in brush and peering through leaves with widening eyes.

storyboard.claim: Huck recognizes the voices, so the fantasy shatters instantly.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Huck crouched in brush, eyes widening in recognition.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The approaching figures are about to be named.
storyboard.addedInformation: Huck's recognition is the turn from fear to certainty.

image.subject: Three men on a dusk graveyard path: a ragged, unkempt man in his forties with a grizzled beard and a torn grey shirt, a young doctor in a dark frock coat carrying a leather bag, and a gaunt dark-haired man in a torn brown coat and slouch hat with a cold, unblinking stare.

storyboard.claim: The figures are Muff Potter, young Dr. Robinson and Injun Joe, real humans not devils.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Three named adults on a graveyard path at dusk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The lantern figures are revealed as people.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces the three adults and their roles.

image.subject: A fresh mound of dark earth beside an open grave at midnight, a spade stuck upright in the dirt, a lantern set on the grass beside a leaning wooden marker.

storyboard.claim: A respected town doctor is robbing a grave.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A spade in fresh earth beside an open grave at midnight.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The voices turn out to be grave robbers.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the grave robbery without showing the body.

image.subject: An 1840s physician's study with leather-bound anatomy books on a shelf, a bare skeleton on a wooden stand and a single candle burning on a writing desk.

storyboard.claim: Medical science advanced, but the legal supply of cadavers was almost nonexistent.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An 1840s anatomy study with books and a skeleton.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The grave robbery is now explained by medical need.
storyboard.addedInformation: Explains why doctors needed bodies.

image.subject: A shadowy man in a long coat counting silver coins into the palm of a grave-digger beside a wooden picket fence at night, a lantern on the ground between them.

storyboard.claim: Doctors paid resurrection men, grave robbers, to dig up fresh bodies.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Coins passed to a grave-digger beside a fence at night.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The anatomy need becomes a payment.
storyboard.addedInformation: The underground trade is shown as a bargain.

image.subject: An open pine coffin lid leaning against a wooden picket fence in a churchyard at dawn, a shovel stuck in the turned earth beside it.

storyboard.claim: Grave robbers dig up freshly buried bodies to study anatomy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A coffin lid leaning on a fence beside a shovel in turned earth.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the economy of the grave trade.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the aftermath of a dig, not the body.

image.subject: A worn ledger open on a counting table, a pile of coins beside a pair of calloused hands, a candle guttering in a dim back room.

storyboard.claim: The underground economy is driven by greed and desperation.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A ledger, coins and calloused hands in a dim room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The payment is now framed as an economy.
storyboard.addedInformation: Greed and desperation are shown through money and hands.

left.label: MUFF DEMANDS
left.subject: A ragged, unkempt man in his forties with a grizzled beard, torn grey shirt, holding out an open hand and demanding more money in a dim alley.

right.label: DOCTOR REFUSES
right.subject: A young doctor in a dark frock coat turning away with a stern face, one hand gripping a heavy wooden plank in the lantern light.

storyboard.claim: A fight over money breaks out between Muff Potter and the doctor.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A demanding man and a refusing doctor, with the doctor holding a plank.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The grave-robbing economy turns into a quarrel.
storyboard.addedInformation: The argument over money is the spark.

image.subject: A gaunt, dark-haired man in his thirties in a torn, dirty brown coat and slouch hat, a hard face with a scar and an unshaven jaw, half-hidden behind a leaning tombstone, a blade catching the lantern light in his hand.

storyboard.claim: Injun Joe, with a long-standing grudge against the doctor's family, jumps in with a knife.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Injun Joe behind a tombstone with a blade catching lantern light.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The argument moves toward the knife.
storyboard.addedInformation: The grudge is shown as Joe's stance and his weapon.

image.subject: A dark empty graveyard at midnight, a lantern lying on its side in the grass beside an open grave, a dropped slouch hat on the ground and a leaning wooden marker in the moonlight.

storyboard.claim: Injun Joe commits cold-blooded murder in front of the boys.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An empty graveyard at midnight with a fallen lantern and a dropped hat.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The knife has been raised; the scene is shown as aftermath.
storyboard.addedInformation: The violence is shown through its traces, not its act.

left.label: SUNDAY SCHOOL
left.subject: Children in a bright Sunday school room trading small paper tickets across rows of wooden benches, sunlight through the windows.

right.label: MIDNIGHT
right.subject: A dark graveyard of leaning wooden markers at midnight, lit only by a lantern held low in the grass.

storyboard.claim: The tone whiplashes from church tickets to a midnight murder.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A bright Sunday school beside a dark midnight graveyard.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The murder scene is set against the earlier church world.
storyboard.addedInformation: The shock is shown through the two worlds.

storyboard.claim: Does Twain lose control of the tone with a penny dreadful murder?
storyboard.concreteVisual: A question card on whether the tone breaks.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The tonal whiplash is now a question.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets up the argument that the jarring tone is intentional.

image.subject: A whitewashed picket fence in bright summer sun, the paint peeling in long strips to reveal grey weathered wood beneath, a dusty St. Petersburg street beyond.

storyboard.claim: Twain intentionally rips the mask off St. Petersburg.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A whitewashed fence peeling to grey wood.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The question of tone is answered with a metaphor.
storyboard.addedInformation: The whitewash veneer is literally shown peeling.

storyboard.claim: Violent frontier reality simmers beneath the polite whitewash veneer of the town.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A place card naming St. Petersburg with the frontier beneath.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The peeling fence becomes the town's naming.
storyboard.addedInformation: The town is named as the place hiding violence.

left.label: TOM'S OUTLAW
left.subject: A freckled boy in a paper pirate hat holding a wooden sword, grinning on a sunny street.

right.label: ENGINE JOE
right.subject: A gaunt, dark-haired man in a torn brown coat and slouch hat, a scar on his face, staring coldly from a dark doorway.

storyboard.claim: Tom wants to be a pirate or Robin Hood, but Injun Joe is what a real outlaw looks like.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A boy with a paper pirate hat beside a scarred, cold-eyed man in a slouch hat.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The murder is now set against Tom's fantasy of outlaws.
storyboard.addedInformation: Tom's version of an outlaw is set against the real one.

image.subject: A child's cloth mask and a torn white sheet lying in a dirt road beneath a bare tree at dusk, the costumes of pretending abandoned in the dust.

storyboard.claim: The Halloween spooks are real world consequences of adult greed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A cloth mask and torn sheet in a dusty road at dusk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Tom's costumes and games are now left behind.
storyboard.addedInformation: The mask and sheet stand for the abandoned play.

image.subject: Two barefoot boys running down a dark dirt road away from a graveyard, silhouetted against a low moon, their shapes small against the long road.

storyboard.claim: The ultimate reality check: the boys run for their lives.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two running silhouettes on a dark road under a low moon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The murder leads straight to flight.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the boys' reaction as flight.

image.subject: A rough pine shingle lying on a splintered bench in a dim old tannery, a bent pin beside it and a small dark red stain on the wood, hides and tanning vats in the shadows behind.

storyboard.claim: They make a blood oath to keep silent, writing it on a pine shingle.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A pine shingle and a bent pin on a bench in a tannery.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The flight ends at the tannery.
storyboard.addedInformation: The oath is shown as a prop.

image.subject: Two boys' hands pressed palm to palm over a pine shingle on a tannery bench, the wood's grain and dim light around them.

storyboard.claim: The boys swear they will drop dead if they tell.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two palms pressed together over the shingle.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The blood oath becomes a physical pact.
storyboard.addedInformation: The silence pact is shown as a gesture.

storyboard.claim: Even in the face of horror, there is a community agreement.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A statement card about the agreement.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The oath is named as an agreement.
storyboard.addedInformation: Ties the oath back to the book's theme.

storyboard.claim: Tom and Huck value their own safety over telling the truth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A statement card on safety over truth.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The pact is named as a choice.
storyboard.addedInformation: The moral choice is stated plainly.

image.subject: A crowd of townspeople in dull Sunday clothes gathered at a graveyard gate at dawn, one man pointing down the road with a hand, the group turned toward the town.

storyboard.claim: The town wakes, finds the body and needs someone to blame.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Townspeople at a graveyard gate at dawn, one pointing.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The silence leads to the search for blame.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the town hunting for a scapegoat.

image.subject: A small isolated framed jail of unpainted timber on a dusty town lane, a single barred window, two barefoot boys lingering by a picket fence nearby.

storyboard.claim: Tom and Huck hang around the small isolated framed jail.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A timber jail on a dusty lane with two boys by a fence.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Blame lands on Muff Potter, and the boys go to the jail.
storyboard.addedInformation: The jail is introduced as the place of the innocent man.

image.subject: Two boys' hands pushing a twist of tobacco and a box of matches through the iron bars of a jail window at night, a chain hanging on the wall inside.

storyboard.claim: Consumed with guilt, the boys hand Muff Potter tobacco and matches through the bars.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two small hands passing tobacco and matches through iron bars.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The jail is now the place of guilt.
storyboard.addedInformation: The gifts show the boys' guilt.

image.subject: A ragged, unkempt man in his forties with a grizzled beard and bloodshot eyes, torn grey shirt and stained trousers, sitting on the floor of a jail cell, chained at the wrist, reaching through the bars toward the light.

storyboard.claim: Muff Potter is chained on the ground floor, waiting to be hanged for a murder he did not commit.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Muff Potter chained on a cell floor reaching toward the bars.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The gifts reach the chained man.
storyboard.addedInformation: The chains show the innocent man's captivity.

image.subject: A large grizzled hand stopped at the iron bars of a jail window, the small hands of two boys on the other side, the gap too narrow for the big hand to pass through.

storyboard.claim: Muff notes that his hands are too big to fit through the bars.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A big hand against the bars with two small hands outside.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The gift is now blocked by the bars.
storyboard.addedInformation: The bars make the size of the hand visible.

storyboard.claim: Muff Potter says, Little hands and weak.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A quotation card from Muff Potter.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The bars continue the scene.
storyboard.addedInformation: Muff's words are quoted directly.

storyboard.claim: The boys have helped Muff Potter a little, and would help him more if they could.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A statement card on the boys' small help.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Muff's quote is answered with a statement.
storyboard.addedInformation: The boys' limited help is named.

image.subject: An empty courthouse bench in dim light, a single bar of sunlight across the floorboards and a closed Bible on the railing, the room silent.

storyboard.claim: The lesson is the crushing moral cost of silence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An empty courtroom bench in a bar of light with a closed Bible.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The jail and guilt lead to the courtroom silence.
storyboard.addedInformation: Silence is shown as the empty room.
